facts.text: Wright grew from scattered homesteads in the late 1800s as the Pensacola and Atlantic Railroad opened in 1883, bringing lumber and naval stores to the Panhandle.
Wright’s growth tied to Eglin Air Force Base expansion in the 1930s, as the nearby Valparaiso Bombing and Gunnery Base was renamed Eglin Field in 1937.
By the 1970s, improved roads and utilities turned Wright into a suburban enclave for military and civilian residents.
Wright sits just 5 miles northwest of Fort Walton Beach, placing it within the Crestview–Fort Walton Beach–Destin Metropolitan Statistical Area.
The area’s limestone, sand, and clay strata reflect historic sea‑level changes, making the region vulnerable to coastal processes.
Logging dominated early economy, with sawmills and turpentine camps drawing workers; John Thomas Brooks, a Confederate veteran, homesteaded waterfront property in the 1860s near what is now Wright.
